# Original-source point and path filter oracle

Generated by `pixi run python scripts/qdrant_point_filter_reference.py` from
Qdrant v1.19.0 commit `74f3e85b9473c62560006c043e13737ce6b48412`.
`filters.json` pins source files, extracted units, the compiled scaffold and
Cargo.lock. Python constructs inputs; Rust supplies every expected result.

The existing payload oracle supplies original JSON-path/field/Boolean routines.
This extension executes the point/path arms from `check_payload`, whole-path
`check_is_empty`/`check_is_null`, original Slice validation/check/hash, and the
actual locked siphasher 1.0.3 crate. The adapter replaces storage access with a
single-ID tracker and vector-presence map, uses std HashSet instead of
MaybeArc/AHashSet, and retains the source nested recursion with absent ID and
empty vector storage. Full Qdrant storage/index/planner execution is not claimed.
The internal CustomIdChecker is unconstructed. Canonical numeric/UUID input
transport uses serde untagged enum decoding; it is not a point-ID protocol test.

12,656 rows include 29 expected parse/validation errors, whole-path vs field
any-element distinctions, missing tracker context, present/absent named vectors,
nested negation and minimum conditions. 2,187 rows additionally compare exact
64-bit hashes: byte lengths 0..512 with zero/max/random data, 518 UInt64 IDs and
130 canonical UUIDs. The hash tests do not claim UUID/native UInt64 storage.

Native tests evaluate original cases directly and through payload/ID metadata
where context is available, compare cloned expressions, and test source hashes,
signed native IDs, partitions, collection/storage/snapshot integration. Public
tests use all applicable source cases through actual native-backed Python and
Arrow; tracker-less and hash-only cases remain native tests.

`dependencies.json` records archive checksums verified against Qdrant Cargo.lock,
extracted source bytes checked against those archives, revisions and notices.
